0.long_answer: Approximately half of the patients with essential thrombocythemia show a mutation in the JAK2 gene. This mutation, most commonly the V617F mutation, results in a change from valine to phenylalanine at position 617. JAK2 is a member of the Janus kinase family and plays a key role in the JAK/STAT signaling pathway, which regulates blood cell production. The mutated form leads to hyperactive signaling that contributes to the abnormal overproduction of platelets, characteristic of essential thrombocythemia.
